source_text:
Ἀδελφοί, οὕτως δεῖ ἡμᾶς φρονεῖν περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς περὶ θεοῦ, ὡς περὶ κριτοῦ ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν: καὶ οὐ δεῖ ἡμᾶς μικρὰ φρονεῖν περὶ τῆς σωτηρίας ἡμῶν.
ἐν τῷ γὰρ φρονεῖν ἡμᾶς μικρὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ, μικρὰ καὶ ἐλπίζομεν λαβεῖν: καὶ οἱ ἀκούοντες ὡς περὶ μικρῶν ἁμαρτάνουσιν, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἁμαρτάνομεν οὐκ εἰδότες, πόθεν ἐκλήθημεν καὶ ὑπὸ τίνος καὶ εἰς ὃν τόπον, καὶ ὅσα ὑπέμεινεν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς παθεῖν ἕνεκα ἡμῶν.
τίνα οὖν ἡμεῖς αὐτῷ δώσομεν ἀντιμισθίαν, ἢ τίνα καρπὸν ἄξιον οὖ ἡμῖν αὐτὸς ἔδωκεν; πόσα δὲ αὐτῷ ὀφείλομεν ὅσια;
τὸ φῶς γὰρ ἡμῖν ἐχαρίσατο, ὡς πατὴρ υἱοὺς ἡμᾶς προσηγόρευσεν, ἀπολλυμένους ἡμᾶς ἔσωσεν.
ποῖον οὖν αἶνον αὐτῷ δώσομεν ἡ μισθὸν ἀντιμισθίας ὦν ἐλάβομεν;
πηροὶ ὄντες τῇ διανοίᾳ, προσκυνοῦντες λίθους καὶ ξύλα καὶ χρυσὸν καὶ ἄργυρον καὶ χαλκόν, ἔργα ἀνθρώπων: καὶ ὁ βίος ἡμῶν ὅλος ἄλλο οὐδὲν ἦν εἰ μὴ θάνατος. ἀμαύρωσιν οὖν περικείμενοι καὶ τοιαύτης ἀχλύος γέμοντες ἐν τῇ ὁράσει, ἀνεβλέψαμεν ἀποθέμενοι ἐκεῖνο ὃ περικείμεθα νέφος τῇ αὐτοῦ θελήσει.
ἠλέησεν γὰρ ἡμᾶς καὶ σπλαγχνισθεὶς ἔσωσεν, θεασάμενος ἐν ἡμῖν πολλὴν πλάνην καὶ ἀπώλειαν, καὶ μηδεμίαν ἐλπίδα ἔχοντας σωτηρίας, εἰ μὴ τὴν παῤ αὐτοῦ.
ἐκάλεσεν γὰρ ἡμᾶς οὐκ ὄντας καὶ ἠθέλησεν ἐκ μὴ ὄντος εἶναι ἡμᾶς.
thought_title: Think of Christ as God and judge; repay his mercy
orientation: The preacher opens his homily by addressing the congregation as brothers, urging them to think rightly about Jesus Christ and about their own salvation.
pass_a_gloss: Brothers, thus it is necessary for us to think about Jesus Christ, as about God, as about judge of living and dead; and it is not necessary for us to think small things about our salvation. For in our thinking small things about him, small things also we hope to receive; and those who hear as about small things sin, and we sin not knowing whence we were called and by whom and into what place, and how many things Jesus Christ endured to suffer for our sake. What recompense therefore shall we give to him, or what fruit worthy of what he himself gave to us? And how many holy things do we owe to him? For the light he granted to us, as a father he addressed us as sons, us who were perishing he saved. What praise therefore shall we give to him or what wage of recompense for what we received? Being blind in the mind, worshipping stones and wood and gold and silver and bronze, works of men; and our whole life was nothing other than death. Therefore being wrapped in dimness and full of such mist in our sight, we looked up, having put off that cloud which we were wrapped in, by his will. For he had mercy on us and being moved with compassion he saved us, having seen in us much error and destruction, and having no hope of salvation, except the one from him. For he called us when we were not, and he willed us to be from not being.

lemmas.gloss: to think, to have in mind
holy things, things owed to God

choices.why: Keeps the literal force of 'small things' as the object of thinking, preserving the contrast with thinking of Christ as God and judge.
Glossary term; renders the idea of a return given in exchange for what was received.
Literal rendering of the dative of respect, showing the blindness was mental or spiritual, not physical.
Keeps the metaphor of being clothed or wrapped in darkness, matching the following 'cloud' image.

choices.english: he willed us to be from not being
choices.why: Preserves the philosophical force of creation from non-being, a key early Christian phrase.
rejected: he willed us to exist from nothing
he willed that we should be from non-existence

pass_b_english: Brothers, this is how we ought to think about Jesus Christ: as God, and as the judge of the living and the dead. And we must not think small things about our salvation.

For when we think small things about him, we also hope to receive small things. And those who hear about these things as if they were small commit sin, and we ourselves sin because we do not know where we were called from, or by whom, or into what place, or how much Jesus Christ endured to suffer for our sake.
What recompense, then, will we give him? What fruit worthy of what he himself has given us? How many holy things do we owe him?
He granted us the light. As a father he called us sons. When we were perishing, he saved us.
What praise, then, will we give him, or what wage of recompense for the things we have received?

We were blind in the mind, worshiping stones and wood and gold and silver and bronze, the works of human hands. And our whole life was nothing other than death. So, wrapped in dimness and full of such mist in our sight, we regained our sight when we put off that cloud that wrapped us, by his will.
For he had mercy on us, and being moved with compassion he saved us, seeing in us much error and destruction, and seeing that we had no hope of salvation except the hope that comes from him.
For he called us when we did not exist, and he willed us into existence from nothing.
